title: A sufficiently positive ample twist of a coherent module is globally generated
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module in the absolute sense of Stacks Definition 01PS [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] (invertible as in [def-sc-invertible-module]), and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ for the $d$-fold tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then there is an integer $d_0$ such that $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] for every $d\ge d_0$; this means that for some finite family of global sections the evaluation map from the direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_X$ indexed by the family onto $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is a sheaf epimorphism.

source.place: EGA II, Proposition 4.5.5, implication 'L ample ⇒ d)' (last paragraph of the proof); equivalently Stacks Properties, Proposition 01Q3 (label proposition-characterize-ample), (1) ⇒ (7)

proof.text: *Notation; $X$ is quasi-compact and separated.* For $n\ge0$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ let $X_s=\{x:\ s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. By condition (1) of that definition $X$ is quasi-compact, and by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated] $X$ is separated, i.e. separated over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Hence $X$ satisfies the hypothesis 'quasi-compact, separated over an affine scheme' of [lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators], for every invertible module on $X$ and every global section of it. (In EGA a 'schéma' is separated by convention, so EGA II 4.5.3 builds this into the definition; with the Stacks definition it is Lemma 09MP.)

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS and Lemma 09MP (lemma-ample-separated); EGA II 4.5.3 (X 'schéma quasi-compact')

proof.text: *A finite affine covering by loci of sections of one tensor power.* By condition (2) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] every $x\in X$ lies in an affine open $X_s$ with $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$; these opens cover $X$, and by quasi-compactness finitely many do: $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$ with $U_i=X_{f_i}$ affine, $f_i\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n_i})$, $n_i\ge1$. Put $m=n_1n_2\cdots n_r\ge1$ and $g_i=f_i^{\otimes m/n_i}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ (tensor powers of sections, using the canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal L^{\otimes a}\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes b}\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes a+b}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]). Then $X_{g_i}=X_{f_i}=U_i$: at a point $x$ choose a generator $e$ of the free rank-one $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $(\mathcal L^{\otimes n_i})_x$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and write $(f_i)_x=ae$; then $(g_i)_x=a^{m/n_i}e^{\otimes m/n_i}$ with $e^{\otimes m/n_i}$ a generator of $(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})_x$, and $a^{k}\notin\mathfrak m_x$ iff $a\notin\mathfrak m_x$ because $\mathfrak m_x$ is a prime ideal. So, as EGA says, replacing the $f_i$ by suitable powers does not change the $X_{f_i}$ and makes all degrees equal to one integer $m$.

source.place: EGA II, proof of Proposition 4.5.5 ('Considérons un recouvrement fini de X par des X_{f_i} ... tous les n_i égaux à un même entier m'); Stacks Properties 01PT (X_{s^n}=X_s)

proof.text: *Local generators.* Let $\mathcal G$ be any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Both properties are local on $X$, so $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module of finite type on the affine scheme $U_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] there are finitely many sections $h_{i1},\dots,h_{ik_i}\in\mathcal G(U_i)$ that generate $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$, i.e. $\mathcal O_{U_i}^{\oplus k_i}\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_ja_jh_{ij}$, is surjective as a map of sheaves.

source.place: EGA II, proof of Proposition 4.5.5 ('Le faisceau F|X_{f_i}, étant de type fini ..., est engendré par un nombre fini de ses sections h_{ij} au-dessus de X_{f_i} (I, 1.3.13)')

proof.text: *Extending the generators after a twist.* The module $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is invertible (locally $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O$, hence $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}\cong\mathcal O^{\otimes m}=\mathcal O$ locally [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and $U_i=X_{g_i}$ is the complement of the zero locus of $g_i$ (the points where the value $g_i(x)\in(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ is nonzero). Apply [lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators] (hypotheses checked in Step 1) to the invertible module $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$, its section $g_i$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ and $t=h_{ij}\in\mathcal G(X_{g_i})$: there are $k_{ij}\ge0$ and $u_{ij}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk_{ij}})$ with $u_{ij}|_{U_i}=h_{ij}\otimes g_i^{k_{ij}}|_{U_i}$ (identifying $(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})^{\otimes k}=\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}$). Let $k_0(\mathcal G)=\max_{i,j}k_{ij}$ (a finite maximum). For every $k\ge k_0(\mathcal G)$ put $u^{(k)}_{ij}=u_{ij}\otimes g_i^{k-k_{ij}}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk})$; then $u^{(k)}_{ij}|_{U_i}=h_{ij}\otimes g_i^{k}|_{U_i}$. (EGA: 'a fortiori les $h_{ij}\otimes f_i^{\otimes k}$ se prolongent ... pour tout $k\ge k_0$'.)

source.place: EGA II, proof of Proposition 4.5.5 ('il existe donc un entier k_0 tel que la section h_{ij}⊗f_i^{⊗k_0} se prolonge en une section de F(k_0 m) au-dessus de X (I, 9.3.1)'); Stacks Properties, Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections)

proof.text: *Global generation of $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}$ for $k\ge k_0(\mathcal G)$.* Fix $k\ge k_0(\mathcal G)$. Since $X_{g_i^{k}}=X_{g_i}=U_i$ (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] applied to the invertible module $\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}$ and its section $g_i^k$ shows that $\mathcal O_{U_i}\to\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}|_{U_i}$, $a\mapsto a\,g_i^k$, is an isomorphism; tensoring with $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\to(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk})|_{U_i}$, $t\mapsto t\otimes g_i^k$, which sends $h_{ij}$ to $u^{(k)}_{ij}|_{U_i}$. An isomorphism carries a surjection $\mathcal O_{U_i}^{\oplus k_i}\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ to a surjection, so the $u^{(k)}_{ij}|_{U_i}$ ($j=1,\dots,k_i$) generate $(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk})|_{U_i}$. Now let $\sigma:\bigoplus_{(i,j)}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}$ be the map of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] for the finite family of all $u^{(k)}_{ij}$. For a section $t$ over an open $V$, on each $V\cap U_i$ the section $t$ is locally of the form $\sum_ja_ju^{(k)}_{ij}$ (the summands indexed by $i$ already suffice), and the $V\cap U_i$ cover $V$; so $\sigma$ is surjective as a map of sheaves, i.e. $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}$ is generated by finitely many global sections, for every $k\ge k_0(\mathcal G)$.

source.place: EGA II, proof of Proposition 4.5.5 ('pour ces valeurs de k, F(km) est donc engendré par ses sections au-dessus de X')

proof.text: *All large twists of $\mathcal F$.* Here $m$ and the covering depend only on $\mathcal L$, not on $\mathcal G$. For $p=0,1,\dots,m-1$ the module $\mathcal G_p=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes p}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type: on an open $W$ where $\mathcal L|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ [def-sc-invertible-module] one has $\mathcal G_p|_W\cong\mathcal F|_W\otimes\mathcal O_W^{\otimes p}\cong\mathcal F|_W$, and both properties are local [pqf-def-coherent]. By Steps 3–5 applied to $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_p$ there is $k_p=k_0(\mathcal G_p)$ such that $\mathcal G_p\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes mk}\cong\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes p+mk}$ is generated by finitely many global sections for all $k\ge k_p$ (an isomorphism transports generating sections). Put $K=\max_pk_p$ and $d_0=mK$. Every $d\ge d_0$ is $d=mk+p$ with $0\le p<m$; then $mk>d-m\ge mK-m$, so $k\ge K\ge k_p$, and $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections.

source.place: EGA II, proof of Proposition 4.5.5 ('Pour tout p tel que 0<p<m, F(p) est aussi de type fini ... car un tel n s'écrit n=km+p avec k≥k_p et 0≤p<m')

proof_origin.place: EGA II, Proposition 4.5.5, proof that an ample L satisfies d) (p. 85); same route as Stacks Properties 01Q3 via 01PW

split_report.summary: The statement cited def-sc-ample, which is defined only for proper schemes over a field (some power very ample) and does not fit an arbitrary scheme X nor the citer (X projective over a complete Noetherian ring A); replaced by a new definition node def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module (absolute ampleness, Stacks 01PS / EGA II 4.5.3), and added def-pc-scheme and def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product to stmt_deps; 'finitely many' global sections made explicit (def-weil-pbc-generating-sections is for finite families). Proof written in six steps following EGA II Prop. 4.5.5 (the direct route: finite affine cover by X_{f_i} of one common degree m, local finite generators, clearing denominators, residues mod m), which is the same argument as Stacks 01Q3 (1)⇒(5)⇒(7) without the detour through L^n globally generated and Modules 01BB. Reused lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators (Stacks 01PW, closed Lean exists_tensorPowSection_eq_restrict on slopmaster2), lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes; created def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module, lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated (Stacks 09MP), lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections (Stacks 01PB + 01IA, EGA I 1.3.13), all searched in Mathlib with no match.
